Then the people learned of his return, so they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we heard of your messenger, so we went out to meet him, to honour him, and to pay him what we owed of the right of Allah. Then he changed his mind about coming and turned back on the road. We feared that what turned him back from the road was a letter that came from you because of an anger you felt against us. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and the anger of His Messenger.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then suspected them, and he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid secretly with an army, ordering him to keep his coming hidden from them, and said to him: 'Look: if you see from them what indicates their faith, take from them the zakat of their wealth; but if you do not see that, then deal with them as you deal with the disbelievers.' Khalid did so, and he reached them and heard from them the adhan for the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. He took their sadaqat from them, and saw from them nothing but obedience and good. He returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news. Then there was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, if a sinful person brings you a report, verify it⦈ [the verse]."

Al-Naba' is the news that is absent from the one who reports it, when it is of significance. Al-Tabayyun is seeking to clarify its reality and to comprehend it with knowledge.

Here there is a subtle benefit: He, glory be to Him, did not command the rejection of the report of the sinner, its denial, or the rejection of his testimony altogether. Rather He commanded verification (tabayyun). If there are indications and evidence from outside that point to its truth, then the evidence of truthfulness is acted upon, even if one who is unreliable reports it. Thus it is proper to rely on the narration and testimony of a sinner. Many sinners speak truthfully in their reports, narrations and testimonies; indeed many of them strive for truthfulness to the utmost, and their sin is in other respects. Such a person's report and testimony are not rejected. If the testimony and narration of such a person were rejected, most rights would be suspended and many authentic reports would be lost, especially when someone's sin is due to belief or opinion while he is striving for truthfulness. Such a person's report and testimony are not rejected.

As for one whose sin is due to lying: if lying is frequent and repeated, to the extent that his lying prevails over his truthfulness, then his report and testimony are not accepted. If he has lied only once or twice, then the scholars have two opinions regarding the rejection of his testimony and report for that reason, and these are two narrations from Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

(Benefit)

Asbagh ibn al-Faraj said: If a sinner gives testimony before a judge, the judge is obliged to suspend judgement in the case. He may be supported in this by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿If a sinful person brings you a report, verify it⦈ [al-Hujurat: 6].

The core of the question is that the basis for accepting or rejecting testimony rests on the predominance of the presumption of truthfulness or its absence.

The correct position, which is decided upon, is that justice (al-'adalah) is divisible: a man may be just in one matter and sinful in another. So when it becomes clear to the judge that he is just concerning what he testifies to, his testimony is accepted and his sin in other matters does not harm it.

Whoever knows the conditions of justice and knows what people are upon will find the correct position in this question clear. And Allah knows best.

He, glorified is He, says: Your love for faith, your desire for it, and its adornment in your hearts did not come from you. Rather, it was Allah who placed it in your hearts in that way, so you preferred it and were pleased with it. Therefore, do not put yourselves forward before My Messenger, and do not speak until he speaks, and do not act until he commands. The One who made faith beloved to you knows better than you what is good for His servants. Without His tawfiq (divine enablement) for you, your souls would not have submitted to faith. Faith did not come about through your own counsel or the success of your own selves, nor did you reach it by your own initiative. Your souls fall short and are unable to reach that. If My Messenger obeyed you in much of what you desire, that would be hard on you, you would perish, your welfare would be corrupted, and you would not perceive it. Do not think that your souls desire for you right guidance and goodness as I desired faith for you. If I had not made it beloved to you, adorned it in your hearts, and made its opposite hateful to you, it would not have occurred from you, and your souls would not have permitted it.

This love and this aversion were not in the soul, nor from it. Rather, it is Allah who bestowed them by His favor, and by them He made the servant among those rightly guided.

﴿Bounty from Allah and a favor; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

(ʿAlīm, All-Knowing) of who is fit for this bounty, who grows through it and upon it, and who bears fruit with Him.

(Ḥakīm, All-Wise), so He does not place it with other than its people, which would waste it by putting it in other than its proper place.

He said in *Shifāʾ al-ʿAlīl*:

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿But know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in distress. But Allah has made faith beloved to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided.﴾

His, glorified is He, making faith beloved to His believing servants is casting His love into their hearts, and no one other than Him can do this. As for a servant making something beloved to another, it is only by adorning it, mentioning its qualities, and what calls to loving it. So He, glorified is He, informed that He placed in the hearts of His believing servants both matters: His love and its goodness, which calls to loving it, and He cast into their hearts aversion to its opposite: disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion. This is purely His favor and grace upon them, since He did not leave them to themselves but Himself undertook this making-beloved, this adornment, and this making-hateful of its opposite, bestowing it upon them as a favor and bounty from Him. Allah is All-Knowing of the locations of His favor, of who is fit for it and who is not, and All-Wise in placing it in its proper places.

[Section: Fusuq (Moral Transgression)]

As for *fusuq* (moral transgression), it occurs in the Book of Allah in two forms: unqualified and singular, and conjoined with *ʿiṣyān* (disobedience).

The singular form is also of two kinds: *fusuq* of disbelief, which takes one out of Islam, and *fusuq* which does not take one out of Islam. The conjoined form is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided.﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 7].

The singular form that is *fusuq* of disbelief is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By it He misguides many and by it He guides many, and He misguides by it none except the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26], and so on.

And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And We have sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 99].

And His saying: ﴿As for those who committed fusuq, their refuge is the Fire. Whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Sajdah: 20], and so on.

All of this is *fusuq* of disbelief.

As for the *fusuq* that does not take one out of Islam, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you do it, indeed it is a *fusuq* in you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], and so on,

and His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if a *fāsiq* (defiant transgressor) comes to you with news﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 6], and so on.

The intended point is mention of the *fusuq* that does not lead to disbelief.

The *fusuq* from which repentance is obligatory is more general than the *fusuq* by which a narration or testimony is rejected.

Our discussion now concerns what repentance is obligatory from, and it is of two kinds: *fusuq* from the side of action, and *fusuq* from the side of belief.

*Fusuq* of action is of two kinds: conjoined with disobedience, and singular.

The conjoined one is committing what Allah has forbidden, and disobedience (*ʿiṣyān*) is disobedience to His command, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6].

And Mūsā said to his brother Hārūn, peace be upon them both: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you then disobey my command?﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 92]. And the poet said:

*I commanded you a firm command, but you disobeyed me, so you became deprived of authority, regretful.*

Thus *fusuq* is more specific to committing the prohibited, and for this reason it is often applied to it, as in His saying: ﴿And if you do it, indeed it is a *fusuq* in you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. And *maʿṣiyah* (disobedience) is more specific to violating the command, as already mentioned. Each of the two is applied to the other, as in His saying: ﴿Except Iblīs, who was of the jinn and so departed (*fasaqa*) from the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

So He named his violation of the command *fusuq*. And He said: ﴿And Ādam disobeyed (*ʿaṣā*) his Lord and went astray﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 121].

So He named his committing of the prohibition *maʿṣiyah*. This is the case when they occur separately. When they are conjoined, one of them refers to violating the command and the other to violating the prohibition.

*Taqwā* (God-consciousness) is guarding against both together, and by realizing it, repentance from *fusuq* and disobedience is valid, by the servant acting in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and abstaining from disobedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.

*Fusuq* of belief is like the *fusuq* of the people of *bidʿah* (innovation) who believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day, and forbid what Allah has forbidden, and obligate what Allah has obligated, but they negate much of what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, out of ignorance, interpretation, and imitation of their shaykhs, and they affirm what Allah and His Messenger did not affirm in the same way.

These are like the Khawārij who passed through (the religion), much of the Rawāfiḍ, the Qadariyyah, the Muʿtazilah, and many of the Jahmiyyah, who were not extremists in *tajahhum* (Jahmī denial of divine attributes).

As for the extreme Jahmiyyah, they are like the extremist Rawāfiḍ. Neither of the two groups has any share in Islam.

He, glorified is He, says: Your love for faith, your desire for it, and its adornment in your hearts did not come from you. Rather, it was Allah who placed it in your hearts in that way, so you preferred it and were pleased with it. Therefore, do not put yourselves forward before My Messenger, and do not speak until he speaks, and do not act until he commands. The One who made faith beloved to you knows better than you what is good for His servants. Without His tawfiq (divine enablement) for you, your souls would not have submitted to faith. Faith did not come about through your own counsel or the success of your own selves, nor did you reach it by your own initiative. Your souls fall short and are unable to reach that. If My Messenger obeyed you in much of what you desire, that would be hard on you, you would perish, your welfare would be corrupted, and you would not perceive it. Do not think that your souls desire for you right guidance and goodness as I desired faith for you. If I had not made it beloved to you, adorned it in your hearts, and made its opposite hateful to you, it would not have occurred from you, and your souls would not have permitted it.

This love and this aversion were not in the soul, nor from it. Rather, it is Allah who bestowed them by His favor, and by them He made the servant among those rightly guided.

﴿Bounty from Allah and a favor; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

(ʿAlīm, All-Knowing) of who is fit for this bounty, who grows through it and upon it, and who bears fruit with Him.

(Ḥakīm, All-Wise), so He does not place it with other than its people, which would waste it by putting it in other than its proper place.

He said in *Shifāʾ al-ʿAlīl*:

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿But know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in distress. But Allah has made faith beloved to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided.﴾

His, glorified is He, making faith beloved to His believing servants is casting His love into their hearts, and no one other than Him can do this. As for a servant making something beloved to another, it is only by adorning it, mentioning its qualities, and what calls to loving it. So He, glorified is He, informed that He placed in the hearts of His believing servants both matters: His love and its goodness, which calls to loving it, and He cast into their hearts aversion to its opposite: disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion. This is purely His favor and grace upon them, since He did not leave them to themselves but Himself undertook this making-beloved, this adornment, and this making-hateful of its opposite, bestowing it upon them as a favor and bounty from Him. Allah is All-Knowing of the locations of His favor, of who is fit for it and who is not, and All-Wise in placing it in its proper places.

[Section: Fusuq (Moral Transgression)]

As for *fusuq* (moral transgression), it occurs in the Book of Allah in two forms: unqualified and singular, and conjoined with *ʿiṣyān* (disobedience).

The singular form is also of two kinds: *fusuq* of disbelief, which takes one out of Islam, and *fusuq* which does not take one out of Islam. The conjoined form is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, defiant disobedience, and rebellion hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided.﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 7].

The singular form that is *fusuq* of disbelief is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By it He misguides many and by it He guides many, and He misguides by it none except the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26], and so on.

And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And We have sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 99].

And His saying: ﴿As for those who committed fusuq, their refuge is the Fire. Whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Sajdah: 20], and so on.

All of this is *fusuq* of disbelief.

As for the *fusuq* that does not take one out of Islam, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you do it, indeed it is a *fusuq* in you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], and so on,

and His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if a *fāsiq* (defiant transgressor) comes to you with news﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 6], and so on.

The intended point is mention of the *fusuq* that does not lead to disbelief.

The *fusuq* from which repentance is obligatory is more general than the *fusuq* by which a narration or testimony is rejected.

Our discussion now concerns what repentance is obligatory from, and it is of two kinds: *fusuq* from the side of action, and *fusuq* from the side of belief.

*Fusuq* of action is of two kinds: conjoined with disobedience, and singular.

The conjoined one is committing what Allah has forbidden, and disobedience (*ʿiṣyān*) is disobedience to His command, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6].

And Mūsā said to his brother Hārūn, peace be upon them both: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you then disobey my command?﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 92]. And the poet said:

*I commanded you a firm command, but you disobeyed me, so you became deprived of authority, regretful.*

Thus *fusuq* is more specific to committing the prohibited, and for this reason it is often applied to it, as in His saying: ﴿And if you do it, indeed it is a *fusuq* in you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. And *maʿṣiyah* (disobedience) is more specific to violating the command, as already mentioned. Each of the two is applied to the other, as in His saying: ﴿Except Iblīs, who was of the jinn and so departed (*fasaqa*) from the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

So He named his violation of the command *fusuq*. And He said: ﴿And Ādam disobeyed (*ʿaṣā*) his Lord and went astray﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 121].

So He named his committing of the prohibition *maʿṣiyah*. This is the case when they occur separately. When they are conjoined, one of them refers to violating the command and the other to violating the prohibition.

*Taqwā* (God-consciousness) is guarding against both together, and by realizing it, repentance from *fusuq* and disobedience is valid, by the servant acting in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and abstaining from disobedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.

*Fusuq* of belief is like the *fusuq* of the people of *bidʿah* (innovation) who believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day, and forbid what Allah has forbidden, and obligate what Allah has obligated, but they negate much of what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, out of ignorance, interpretation, and imitation of their shaykhs, and they affirm what Allah and His Messenger did not affirm in the same way.

These are like the Khawārij who passed through (the religion), much of the Rawāfiḍ, the Qadariyyah, the Muʿtazilah, and many of the Jahmiyyah, who were not extremists in *tajahhum* (Jahmī denial of divine attributes).

As for the extreme Jahmiyyah, they are like the extremist Rawāfiḍ. Neither of the two groups has any share in Islam.

**[Reconciliation (ṣulḥ) Among the Muslims]**

His saying: "Reconciliation (ṣulḥ) is permissible among the Muslims, except a reconciliation that makes lawful what is forbidden or makes forbidden what is lawful." This is related from the Prophet (ﷺ), narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others, from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Muzani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

«Reconciliation is permissible among the Muslims, except a reconciliation that makes forbidden what is lawful or makes lawful what is forbidden. The Muslims are bound by their conditions, except a condition that makes forbidden what is lawful or makes lawful what is forbidden.»

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sound (ṣaḥīḥ) hadith." Allah, glorified and exalted, has urged reconciliation between two groups in cases of bloodshed, saying:

﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them.﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]

He also urged the spouses to reconcile when they dispute over their rights, saying: ﴿And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make a settlement between themselves; and settlement is best.﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 128]

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity or what is right or reconciliation between people.﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 114]

The Prophet (ﷺ) made reconciliation between the clans of ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf when a dispute arose between them. When Kaʿb ibn Mālik and Ibn Abī Ḥadrad disputed over a debt owed by Ibn Abī Ḥadrad, the Prophet (ﷺ) made peace by asking Kaʿb to reduce half of his debt, and he instructed the debtor to pay the other half. He also said to two men who had brought their dispute before him:

«Go and divide (the property) equally, then seek out what is right, then draw lots, then each of you should absolve his companion.»

He also said: «Whoever has a wrong committed against his brother, whether concerning his honour or anything else, let him seek his absolution from him today, before there is no dinar or dirham (to pay with). If he has good deeds, some of them will be taken from him in proportion to his wrong; and if he has no good deeds, some of the sins of his companion will be taken and placed upon him.»

He permitted, in the case of intentional killing (dam al-ʿamd), that the heirs of the slain may accept what they agree upon (as compensation). When ʿAbd Allah ibn Ḥarām al-Anṣārī, the father of Jābir, was martyred, and he had a debt, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his creditors to accept the produce of his orchard and to absolve his father.

ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhumā) that he did not see any harm in al-mukhāraja, meaning reconciliation in inheritance. It is called al-mukhāraja because the heir is given what he agrees to take, and thereby removes himself from the inheritance. The wife of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf reconciled regarding her share of the one-eighth (of the estate, from the wife's portion) for eighty thousand (dirhams).

Misʿar reported from Azhar, from Muḥārib, who said: ʿUmar (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) said:

"Send the litigants back until they reconcile, for a decisive judgment creates resentment among the people."

ʿUmar also said: "Send the litigants back so that perhaps they will reconcile, for that is more conducive to truthfulness and less conducive to treachery."

ʿUmar also said: "Send the litigants back if there is kinship between them, for a decisive judgment produces enmity among them."

**[Section: Rights are of two kinds: the right of Allah, the Exalted, and the right of His servants]**

Rights are of two kinds: the right of Allah, and the right of the human being. The right of Allah admits no place for reconciliation, such as the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd), the zakāt, the expiations (kaffārāt) and the like. Reconciliation takes place only between the servant and his Lord in establishing these, not in neglecting them. For this reason, no compromise is accepted regarding the ḥudūd, and when they reach the ruler, Allah curses both the intercessor and the one who is interceded for.

As for the rights of human beings, these are the rights that accept reconciliation, remission and exchange. The just reconciliation is the one that Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) commanded, as He said: ﴿So make peace between them with justice.﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]

The unjust reconciliation is pure oppression itself. Many people do not adhere to justice in reconciliation; rather, they make an oppressive, unjust reconciliation. They reconcile between two debtors by (having one accept) less than a slight portion of one party's right. The Prophet (ﷺ) made reconciliation between Kaʿb and his debtor, and it was the most just reconciliation, when he commanded him to take half and leave half. Likewise, when he (ﷺ) intended to divorce Sawda, she agreed to give up her night to him and to retain her right to maintenance and clothing. This is the most just reconciliation. Allah, glorified, permitted a man to divorce his wife and replace her with another. So when she agrees to forgo part of her right and take part of it, and he keeps her, this is among the just reconciliations.

Likewise, He guided the two disputing parties who had disputes over inheritance to seek the truth to the extent possible, and then each should absolve his companion. Allah, glorified, first commanded making peace between the two fighting groups. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then He commanded fighting the transgressing group, not reconciliation, because it is oppressive. Reconciliation with its oppression involves violating the right of the wronged group. Many oppressive reconcilers make peace between the powerful oppressor and the weak wronged opponent in a way that pleases the powerful man of standing, in which he has an advantage, while the leniency and injustice fall upon the weak. He thinks he has reconciled, but he does not enable the wronged party to take his right. This is oppression. Rather, he should enable the wronged party to obtain his right, and then ask him, with his consent, to forgo part of his right, without favouritism toward the man of standing, and without compelling the other party through favouritism or the like.

**[Section: Reconciliation is either rejected or permissible and binding]**

The reconciliation that makes lawful what is forbidden and forbidden what is lawful is like a reconciliation that involves making unlawful a lawful intimacy (buḍʿ), or making lawful an unlawful intimacy, or enslaving a free person, or transferring a lineage or patronage (walāʾ) from one place to another, or consuming ribā, or dropping an obligation, or suspending a ḥadd, or oppressing a third party, and the like. All of these are reconciliations that are permissible but rejected.

The permissible reconciliation among the Muslims is the one that relies upon the pleasure of Allah, glorified, and the pleasure of the two opponents. This is the most just and most rightful reconciliation. It depends on knowledge and justice. So the reconciler must be knowledgeable about the facts, aware of what is obligatory, and intent on justice. The rank of this person is higher than the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer at night, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

«Shall I not inform you of something more excellent than the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer?» They said: «Yes, O Messenger of Allah.» He said: «Reconciling between people, for the corruption of relations is the shaver (ḥāliqa); I do not mean that it shaves hair, but that it shaves away the religion.»

It has been reported in a narration (athar): "Make peace among the people, for Allah makes peace among the believers on the Day of Resurrection." Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers, and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 10]

(Section: Consoling/Supporting the believer takes many forms.)

Support for the believer (al-muwasah) takes many forms: support with wealth, support with status (al-jah), support with the body and service, support with counsel and guidance, support with supplication and seeking forgiveness for them, and support by sharing their grief.

This support is in proportion to one's faith: as faith weakens, support weakens, and as it grows stronger, support grows stronger.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the greatest of people in supporting his Companions in all of this, so his followers' share of such support is in accordance with their following of him.

They entered upon Bishr al-Hafi on a day of severe cold, and he had stripped down and was shivering. They said, "What is this, O Abu Nasr?"

He said, "I remembered the poor and their cold, and I have nothing with which to support them, so I wanted to share in their cold."

﴿And whoever does not repent, those are the wrongdoers.﴾ He divided the servants into the repentant and the wrongdoers, and there is absolutely no third category. He applied the name "wrongdoer" to whoever does not repent, and there is no greater wrongdoer than such a person, because of his ignorance of his Lord and of his own rights, and of the defects of his soul and the blights of his deeds.

In the Sahih, it is related from him (ﷺ) that he said:

"O people, repent to Allah, for by Allah, I repent to Him more than seventy times a day."

(Benefit)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames.﴾ There is no disagreement on the prohibition of giving a person a nickname that he dislikes, whether or not it applies to him. As for when a person is known by a nickname and it has become famous for him, such as al-A'mash, al-Ashtar, al-Asamm and al-A'raj, its use has been consistent on the tongues of the scholars, past and present, and Imam Ahmad was lenient regarding it.

Abu Dawud said in his Masa'il: I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal being asked about a man who has a nickname by which he is known and which he does not dislike.

He said: "Is it not said, Sulayman al-A'mash and Humayd al-Tawil?"

It seemed that he saw no harm in it.

Abu Dawud said: I asked Ahmad about it again another time, and he permitted it.

I said: Ahmad used to dislike saying "al-A'mash said, Fudayl said," and they claim that he used to say "Sulayman." Either the name conveys neither praise nor blame. If it begins with "Abu" or "Umm," it is a kunya, such as Abu so-and-so or Umm so-and-so. If it does not begin with that, it is a proper name, such as Zayd and 'Amr.

This is what the Arabs knew, and their discourse revolved around it.

As for Fulan al-Din, Izz al-Din, Izz al-Dawla and Baha' al-Dawla, they did not know these, and this only came from the non-Arabs ('Ajam).

(Section)

Know that patience against the sins of the tongue and the private parts is among the hardest kinds of patience, because the call to them is strong and they are easy. The sins of the tongue are the fruit of a person, such as backbiting (namima), slander (ghiba), lying, and disputation, praising oneself, whether by allusion or explicitly, repeating people's words, attacking those one hates, praising those one loves, and the like.

The strength of the call combines with the ease of the tongue's movement, so patience weakens. For this reason he (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh:

"Keep your tongue under control." He said: "Shall we be held accountable for what we speak?" He (ﷺ) said: "Do people get thrown into the Fire on their faces except for the harvest of their tongues?"

This is especially so when sinful speech has become a habit for the servant. Then patience against it becomes very hard for him. For this reason, you find a man who stands in prayer at night and fasts by day, and who avoids resting his back on a silk cushion even for a moment, yet lets his tongue loose in backbiting, slander and mockery of people's honor. Sometimes the righteous and those who know Allah and religion permit saying about Allah what they do not know. Many who are scrupulous about trifles of the unlawful, a drop of wine, or a speck of impurity as small as the head of a pin, do not care about committing unlawful intercourse.

It is related that:

A man was alone with a non-mahram woman, and when he wanted to have intercourse with her, he said: "O woman, cover your face, for looking at the face of a non-mahram woman is unlawful."

A man asked Abdullah ibn Umar about the blood of a mosquito, and he said: "Look at these people, asking me about the blood of a mosquito, while they have killed the son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah!?"

A similar incident happened to me. I was in the state of ihram, and some Bedouins, well known for killing souls and raiding wealth, came to me asking about killing a louse while in ihram.

I said: "How strange! A people who do not scruple at killing a soul that Allah has forbidden to kill, yet ask about killing a louse in ihram."

The point is that the difference in the strength of patience across kinds of sins and individual sins corresponds to the difference in the strength of the call to that sin.

It is related from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said:

"Patience is of three kinds: patience upon calamity, patience upon obedience, and patience against disobedience.

Whoever is patient upon calamity until he meets it with good consolation, Allah writes for him three hundred degrees.

Whoever is patient upon obedience until he performs it as Allah commanded, Allah writes for him six hundred degrees.

Whoever is patient against disobedience out of fear of Allah and hope for what is with Him, Allah writes for him nine hundred degrees."

Maymun ibn Mihran said:

"Patience is two kinds: patience upon calamity is good, and better than it is patience against disobedience."

[Section: Sin is a cause of blame]

Among its punishments is that it strips its doer of the names of praise and honor, and clothes him in the names of blame and disgrace. So it strips him of the names: believer, righteous, doer of good, pious, obedient, penitent, friend (of Allah), scrupulous, upright, worshipper, fearful, returning (to Allah), good, pleasing, and the like.

It clothes him with the names: profligate, disobedient, opponent, evildoer, corrupter, wicked, detested, adulterer, thief, murderer, liar, traitor, sodomite, severer of ties of kinship, treacherous, and the like.

These are the names of wickedness, and ﴿wretched is the name of wickedness after faith﴾, which brings about the anger of the Judge, entry into the Fires, and a life of disgrace and humiliation.

Those are names that bring about the pleasure of the Most Merciful, entry into the Gardens, and bring about for their bearer honor above all kinds of humankind. If the punishment for sin were only the deserving of those names and their consequences, reason would still forbid it. And if the reward of obedience were only the attainment of those names and their consequences, reason would still command it. But there is no preventer of what Allah gives, no giver of what He withholds, no one who brings near what He distances, and no one who distances whom He brings near. ﴿And whoever Allah humiliates, for him there is no honorer. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.﴾ [al-Hajj: 18]

This is one of the finest examples of analogy by illustration (al-qiyas al-tamthili). It likens the tearing of a brother's honour to the tearing of his flesh. Since the backbiter tears his brother's honour in his absence, he is in the position of one who cuts up his flesh while his soul is absent from him through death. And since the backbiter is unable to defend himself by reason of being absent from the one who disparages him, he is in the position of the dead man whose flesh is cut and who cannot repel it from himself. Since the requirement of brotherhood is mercy, kindness and support, and the backbiter has attached to it the opposite of what it requires, namely blame, faultfinding and slander, this is the equivalent of cutting up his brother's flesh. Brotherhood requires guarding him, protecting him and defending him. Since the backbiter takes pleasure in his brother's honour, delighting in his absence and disparagement and adorning himself with that, he is likened to one who eats his brother's flesh after cutting it up. And since the backbiter loves that and is pleased with it, he is likened to one who loves to eat his brother's flesh when he is dead. His love for this is a degree beyond mere eating, just as eating is a degree beyond tearing.

So reflect on this simile and illustration, on the excellence of its placement, and on the correspondence between the intelligible meaning and the sensible image in it. Reflect also on His report about them of their aversion to eating the flesh of a dead brother, and on His describing them with that at the end of the verse, and on the rebuke directed at them at its beginning for one of them loving that. Just as this is hateful to their natures, how then do they love what is like it and its equivalent?

He argued against them with what they hate in order to refute what they love, and He likened what they love to what is most hateful to them, and they are most averse to it. For this reason reason, natural disposition and wisdom require that they be most averse to what is its equivalent and likeness. And success is from God.

(Note: the passage contains a few textual irregularities, such as the parenthesis opened in the Tirmidhi hadith and the unclosed quotation of the Tirmidhi narration; I translate them as they stand.)

**(Benefit)**

As for their discussion of the question of the poor patient person and the wealthy grateful person, and the preference of one of them over the other:

According to the people of verification and knowledge, preference does not return to the essence of poverty and wealth. Rather, it returns to deeds, states, and realities. Thus the question itself is invalid in its own right. Preference before Allah, exalted is He, is by taqwa (God-consciousness) and the realities of faith, not by poverty or wealth, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾.

He did not say "the poorest of you" or "the richest of you."

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, said: Poverty and wealth are a trial from Allah for His servant, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tries him and honors him and bestows favor upon him, he says, "My Lord has honored me." But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No! ﴾

That is, not everyone to whom I expand provision and give is one whom I have honored, nor is everyone whose provision I restrict and constrict one whom I have humiliated. Honor is that Allah honors the servant with obedience to Him, faith in Him, love of Him, and knowledge of Him. Humiliation is that He strips him of these.

He said—meaning Ibn Taymiyyah—and preference does not occur through wealth or poverty.

Rather, it is through taqwa. If they are equal in taqwa, they are equal in rank. I heard him say that.

This question was discussed in the presence of Yahya ibn Mu'adh, and he said: "Poverty and wealth will not be weighed tomorrow; only patience and gratitude will be weighed."

**(Section)**

It has been said: There is no doubt that the child is formed from the father's water just as it is formed from the mother's water, but it came into being and became a valued property in the mother's womb. The parts by which it became so from the mother are many times over the single part from the father, despite their equality in that part. It was formed in her womb from her flesh and blood. When the father deposited it, it had no value at all; rather, it was as Allah called it: "a despised water" with no worth. For this reason, if a man's stallion covered another man's mare, the offspring belongs to the owner of the female by the consensus of the Muslims. This is unlike seed, which is valued property before being placed in the earth, and for which compensation is paid, whereas the stud fee for the stallion is not compensated. So analogizing one to the other is among the most invalid analogies.

If it is said: Why do you not apply this to lineage, and assign it to the mother as you assigned it to the father?

It is said: The Muslims have agreed that lineage belongs to the father, just as they agreed that the child follows the mother in freedom and slavery. This is what Allah's wisdom requires, both in the law and in decree. The father is the one to whom the child is born, while the mother is a vessel, even though it is formed within her. Allah, glorified is He, made the child the successor of his father, his branch, and his substitute, and He placed lineages among His servants, so it is said: "So-and-so son of so-and-so." Their interests, mutual recognition, and transactions are not complete without this, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

Had lineages not been established through the fathers, recognition would not have occurred, and the order of the servants would have been corrupted, for women are veiled and concealed from eyes; it is generally impossible to identify the mother's person so as to testify concerning the child's lineage through her. If lineages were assigned to mothers, they would be lost and corrupted, and that would contradict wisdom, mercy, and benefit. For this reason, people will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their fathers, not by their mothers.

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: "Chapter: People will be called by their fathers on the Day of Resurrection," then he mentioned the hadith: "Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection at his backside according to the measure of his treachery; it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so son of so-and-so.'"

So it is part of the completeness of wisdom that He made freedom and slavery follow the mother, and lineage follow the father. Corrupt analogy only joins what Allah has separated or separates what Allah has joined.

If it is said: Why do you not apply this to walā' (patronage), and assign it to the mother's clients? Walā' is a bond like the bond of lineage.

It is said: Since walā' is a consequence and requirement of slavery, it follows it in its ruling, so it belongs to the mother's clients. Since it has a trace of lineage and is a bond like its bond, it returns to the father's clients when it is cut off from the mother's clients. Thus both matters are observed, and both effects are arranged upon it.

If it is said: Why do you not make the child in religion follow the one who has the lineage, rather than attaching him sometimes to his father and sometimes to his mother?

It is said: The child cannot stand on his own; rather, he can only be a follower of another. So the Lawgiver made him follow the better of his two parents in religion, giving preference to the better of the two religions. For if he has no choice but to follow, it is not permissible for him to follow one who is upon the religion of Satan, and his following be severed from one who is upon the religion of the Merciful. This is impossible in the wisdom and law of Allah, exalted is He.

And he said in (al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an):

They said: The senses testify that the parts in the offspring from the mother are many times over the parts in it from the father.

So it is established that its formation is from the mother's water and the menstrual blood, and the father's water is the coagulant for it, like rennet.

The majority disputed this and said: It is formed from the water of both the man and the woman. Then they have two opinions.

One of them: its limbs and parts come from the male's water, and its form from the female's water.

The second: the limbs, parts, and form were formed from the combination of the two waters, and that they mixed and blended and became one water. This is the correct view, for we find form and shaping sometimes attributed to the father and sometimes to the mother. And Allah knows best.

This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾

The origin is the male. From him comes the seed, and from him the watering.

The female is a vessel and a repository for her offspring. She nurtures it in her womb as she nurtures it in her lap.

For this reason the child belongs to the father in ruling and lineage.

As for its following the mother in freedom and slavery, that is because it was formed and became a child in her womb, and she nourished it with her milk along with the part of it that came from her.

The father has more right to its lineage and its agnatic relation, because he is its origin, its material, and its copy.

And the one of the two who is more honorable in religion has more right to it, giving precedence to the religion and law of Allah.

[Section: On his ruling ﷺ regarding equality (kafa'ah) in marriage]

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

And He said: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 10].

And He said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71].

And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So their Lord responded to them: "Indeed, I will not allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 195].

And the Prophet ﷺ said:

"There is no virtue of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab, nor of a white person over a black person, nor of a black person over a white person, except by taqwa. People are from Adam, and Adam is from dust."

And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, the family of so-and-so are not my allies; indeed, my allies are the righteous, wherever they are and wherever they may be."

And in al-Tirmidhi, from him ﷺ:

"If one comes to you whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him; if you do not do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he has (a defect)?" He said: "If one comes to you whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him," three times.

The Prophet ﷺ said to the Banu Bayadah: "Marry Abu Hind, and marry to him." He was a cupper.

The Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Qurashiyyah to Zayd ibn Harithah, his freedman. He married Fatimah bint Qays al-Fihriyyah al-Qurashiyyah to Usamah, his son.

Bilal ibn Rabah married the sister of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And good women are for good men, and good men are for good women﴾ [al-Nur: 26].

And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿So marry what is good for you of women﴾ [al-Nisa: 3].

What his ruling ﷺ requires is that religion be considered in equality, as a foundation and as perfection. Thus a Muslim woman is not married to a disbeliever, nor a chaste woman to a profligate. The Qur'an and the Sunnah did not consider any matter beyond this in equality, for He forbade the Muslim woman to marry a fornicating, corrupt man, but did not consider lineage, craft, wealth, or freedom. So He permitted a slave to marry a noble, wealthy free woman if he is chaste and Muslim, permitted non-Qurayshis to marry Qurayshi women, non-Hashimis to marry Hashimi women, and the poor to marry wealthy women.

The jurists have disputed the attributes of equality. Malik, in the apparent view of his school, said it is religion alone; in another narration from him, it is three: religion, freedom, and freedom from defects.

Abu Hanifah said: it is lineage and religion.

Ahmad, in one narration from him, said: it is religion and lineage only. In another narration: it is five: religion, lineage, freedom, craft, and wealth. If lineage is considered in it, then there are two narrations from him: one, that Arabs are equal to one another; the second, that Quraysh are equal only to a Qurayshi, and the Banu Hashim are equal only to a Hashimi.

The companions of al-Shafi'i said: religion, lineage, freedom, craft, and freedom from repulsive defects are considered in it.

They have three views regarding wealth: that it is considered in it, that it is disregarded, and that it is considered among city dwellers but not among desert dwellers. Thus, according to them, a non-Arab is not an equal for an Arab, nor a non-Qurayshi for a Qurayshi woman, nor a non-Hashimi for a Hashimi woman, nor one who is not connected to the well-known scholars and righteous for one who is connected to them; nor is a slave an equal for a free woman, nor a freedman an equal for a woman of free origin, nor one who has slavery touching any of his fathers an equal for one whom slavery has not touched, nor any of her fathers; and regarding the influence of the slavery of mothers there are two views. Nor is one who has a defect that establishes the right of annulment an equal for one free of it. If annulment is not established but the defect is repulsive, such as blindness, amputation, or disfigurement of form, then there are two views; al-Ruyani chose that its bearer is not an equal. Nor is a cupper, weaver, or guard an equal for the daughter of a merchant, tailor, or the like; nor is a craftsman an equal for the daughter of a scholar; nor is a sinner an equal for a chaste woman; nor is an innovator an equal for a Sunni woman. However, according to the majority, equality is a right of the woman and the guardians.

Then they differed: the companions of al-Shafi'i said: it belongs to the one who has guardianship at present.

Ahmad, in one narration, said: it is a right of all guardians, near and distant; so whoever of them is not satisfied has the right to annul. Ahmad, in a third narration, said: it is a right of Allah, so their consent to waive it is not valid. But according to this narration, freedom, wealth, craft, and lineage are not considered; only religion is considered. For neither Ahmad nor any scholar said that the marriage of a poor man to a wealthy woman is void even if she consents, nor does he or anyone say that the marriage of a Hashimi woman to a non-Hashimi, or a Qurayshi woman to a non-Qurayshi, is void. We have only drawn attention to this because many of our companions relate the disagreement regarding equality—is it a right of Allah or of the human being?—and they state without qualification that equality consists of the qualities mentioned; and in this there is so much laxity and lack of verification.

(Section heading) (Benefit)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not yet believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

Then He mentioned the description of the people of faith, saying: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.﴾

So assent and obedience do not constitute faith unless they are unrestricted. If they are restricted, then at their highest level, provided they are free of doubt, they are submission (islam), and their possessor is among the common Muslims, not among the elite of the believers.

(Subtle point)

Some of the Companions would recite the talbiyah (the call "Labbayk") abundantly while in ihram, then say, "Labbayk." Had it been mere show (riya'), it would have vanished. Allah the Exalted has negated faith from those who claimed it, and he has no taste for it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not yet believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14].

These are Muslims, not believers, because they are not among those whom faith has touched in their hearts, so that they tasted its sweetness and its flavor. This is the state of most of those who ascribe themselves to Islam. These are not disbelievers, for He, glorified is He, affirmed Islam for them by His saying: ﴿but say, "We have submitted."﴾

And it is not meant: "Say it with your tongues without the agreement of the heart."

For He distinguished between their saying "We have believed" and their saying "We have submitted." But since they had not tasted the flavor of faith, He said: "You have not believed." Yet, along with that, He, glorified and exalted is He, promised them for their obedience that He would not diminish anything of the rewards of their deeds.

Then He mentioned the people of faith who tasted its flavor, and they are those who believed in Him and His Messenger, then did not doubt regarding their faith. What removed doubt from them was that faith had touched their hearts and its cheerfulness had mingled with them, so no place remained in them for doubt.

What confirmed this taste was their expending what is dearest to them for the pleasure of their Lord, the Exalted: namely their wealth and their selves.

And it is impossible that such expenditure should occur without tasting the flavor of faith and experiencing its sweetness. For that is achieved only through true taste and inner perception.

As al-Hasan said: "Faith is not by wishful thinking, nor by adornment, but it is what settles in the heart and is confirmed by deeds."

So taste and inner perception are an inward matter, and deeds are a proof of it and a confirmation of it.

Just as doubt, suspicion and hypocrisy are an inward matter, and deeds are a proof of them and a confirmation of them.

Thus deeds are the fruits of knowledge and beliefs. Certainty bears fruit in striving and in the stations of excellence (ihsan). According to its strength, its fruit and result will be produced. Doubt and suspicion bear the deeds appropriate to them. And success is from Allah.

(Section: The rule of absolute faith and unrestricted faith)

Absolute faith (al-iman al-mutlaq) is applied only to the perfect, the perfection commanded, while unrestricted faith (mutlaq al-iman) is applied to both the deficient and the perfect.

For this reason the Prophet ﷺ negated absolute faith from the fornicator, the wine-drinker and the thief, but did not negate unrestricted faith from him, lest he fall outside His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾, nor His saying: ﴿The believers have certainly succeeded﴾,

nor His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾, through to the end of the verses.

And it enters His saying: ﴿then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, and His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾,

and His saying: "A believer is not to be killed for a disbeliever,"

and similar things.

Therefore His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not yet believed; rather say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ is a negation of absolute faith, not of unrestricted faith, for several reasons:

Among them: He commanded them, or permitted them, to say "We have submitted," and the hypocrite is not told that.

Among them: He said ﴿The Bedouins﴾ and did not say "the hypocrites."

Among them: these were the boorish ones who called out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from behind the private chambers and raised their voices above his voice, out of harshness and boorishness, not out of hypocrisy and disbelief.

Among them: He said ﴿for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, and did not negate the entry of Islam into their hearts. Had they been hypocrites, He would have negated Islam from them as He negated faith.

Among them: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾, i.e., He will not diminish them for you, and the hypocrite has no obedience.

Among them: He said: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have submitted. Say, "Do not consider your submission a favor to me."﴾ So He affirmed their submission and forbade them from considering it a favor upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had it not been valid submission, He would have said "You have not submitted, but you are liars," as He refuted them in their saying: ﴿"We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah,"﴾ since their testimony did not correspond to their belief.

Among them: He said: ﴿Rather, Allah bestows favor upon you﴾, and had they been hypocrites, He would not have bestowed favor upon them.

Among them: He said: ﴿that He guided you to faith﴾. This does not conflict with His saying ﴿Say, "You have not yet believed"﴾, for He negated absolute faith and bestowed favor upon them by guiding them to Islam, which includes unrestricted faith.

Among them: when the Prophet ﷺ divided the distribution, Sa'd said to him: "You gave to so-and-so and left so-and-so, though he is a believer." He said: "Or a Muslim," three times, and affirmed for him Islam without faith.

There are wondrous secrets in the verse, but this is not the place for them. The aim here is the distinction between absolute faith and unrestricted faith: absolute faith prevents entry into the Fire, while unrestricted faith prevents abiding in it forever.

Tenth: When you say "al-amr al-mutlaq" (the absolute command), you have attached the definite article to "amr," which denotes generality and comprehensiveness; then you describe it afterward as "unrestricted," meaning it is not confined by any restriction that would limit it, such as a condition or an attribute or otherwise. So it is general across every individual of the kind that is such.

As for "mutlaq al-amr" (an unrestricted command), the annexation there is not for generality but for specification, so it is a common, unrestricted notion that is true of any one of its instances.

On this basis, "mutlaq al-bay'" (sale in general) is permissible, and "al-bay' al-mutlaq" (the absolute sale) is divided into permissible and otherwise.

"Al-amr al-mutlaq" indicates obligation, while "mutlaq al-amr" is divided into obligatory and recommended.

"Al-ma' al-mutlaq" is pure (tahur), while "mutlaq al-ma'" is divided into pure and other.

"Al-milk al-mutlaq" is that which is established for a free person, while "mutlaq al-milk" is established for a slave.

So if it is said: does a slave own property or not? The correct answer is to affirm unrestricted ownership for him, not absolute ownership.

And if it is asked: is the sinner a believer or not? The answer is according to this detailed distinction. And Allah knows best.

Through this verification the difficulty is removed concerning the question of whether the recommended act is commanded or not, and concerning the question of whether the sinner is a believer or not.

(Principle)

Faith has an outward and an inward aspect. Its outward aspect is the utterance of the tongue and the action of the limbs, and its inward aspect is the assent of the heart, its submission and its love.

An outward aspect without an inward one benefits nothing, even if blood is thereby protected and wealth and offspring are safeguarded.

An inward aspect without an outward one suffices only when it is impossible to perform due to incapacity or compulsion or fear of destruction. The absence of the outward action when there is no obstacle is evidence of the corruption of the inward aspect and its emptiness of faith; its deficiency is evidence of its deficiency, and its strength is evidence of its strength.

Faith is the core and essence of Islam, and certainty is the core and essence of faith. Every knowledge and action that does not increase faith and certainty in strength is corrupted, and every faith that does not impel to action is corrupted.

[Section: Rulings apply to outward appearances]

If it is said: You have lengthened the discussion on the question of intentions in contracts, and we will judge you by the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the sayings of the Imams. Allah the Exalted said, relating about His Prophet Noah: ﴿And I do not say to those whom your eyes despise, that Allah will not grant them any good. Allah knows best what is within themselves. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers.﴾ [Hud: 31]

So He grounded the judgment on the outward appearance of their faith, and referred the knowledge of what is within themselves to the Knower of hidden things, the Exalted, the One alone who knows the essence of what is in the breasts and the knowledge of what is in souls of the unseen. And Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿And I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen﴾ [Hud: 31].

The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have not been commanded to search the hearts of people or to split open their bellies." And he said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say it, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is upon Allah." So he was content with the outward appearance from them, and entrusted their inner states to Allah. He did the same with those who stayed behind and made excuses to him: he accepted their outward profession and entrusted their inner states to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Likewise was his practice with the hypocrites: he accepted the outward aspect of their Islam and left their inner states to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And Allah said: ﴿And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [al-Isra': 36].

He did not make for us knowledge of intentions and purposes upon which worldly rulings depend, so our saying is: we have no knowledge of it.

Al-Shafi'i said: Allah obligated His creation to obey His Prophet and did not give them any share of command. It is even more fitting that they should not presume to pass judgment on the unseen of anyone by inference or conjecture, given the limitation of their knowledge compared with the knowledge of His prophets, whom He obligated to halt at what reached them until His command comes to them. For He made the proofs manifest to them, and He made judgment in this world for them only by what appeared of the one judged. So He obligated His Prophet to fight the people of idols until they submit, so that their blood is protected when they manifest Islam, and He informed him that none knows the truthfulness of their Islam except Allah. Then Allah made His Messenger aware of people who manifest Islam while concealing otherwise, yet He did not give him the right to judge them contrary to the ruling of Islam, nor to decide against them in this world contrary to what they manifested. So He said to His Prophet: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted.'"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]

That is, "We have submitted" by the saying, out of fear of killing and captivity. Then He informed them that He would reward them if they obeyed Allah and His Messenger, that is, if they newly established obedience to Allah and His Messenger. And He said of the hypocrites, who are a second category: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 2], that is, a shield from killing. And He said: ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 95].

So He commanded acceptance of what they manifested, and did not give His Prophet the right to judge against them contrary to the ruling of faith. Allah had informed His Prophet that they are in the lowest level of the Fire. So His judgment upon them is based on their inner states, while the judgment of His Prophet upon them in this world is based on their outward aspect: through manifesting repentance, through what was established by evidence from the Muslims, and through what they confessed by their words, and what they denied of the words of disbelief, when it was not confessed by them and no evidence was established against them. And He refuted them in all of their claims. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ related from Allah. Malik informed us from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Adi ibn al-Khiyar that:

A man whispered to the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not know what he had whispered until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke aloud, and behold, he was consulting him about killing a man among the hypocrites. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Does he not testify that there is no god but Allah?" He said: "Yes, but there is no testimony for him." He said: "Does he not pray?" He said: "Yes, but there is no prayer for him." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Those are the ones whom Allah has forbidden me to kill." Then he mentioned the hadith: "I have been commanded to fight people..." Then he said: Their reckoning is upon Allah, according to their truthfulness and their falsehood, and their inner states are with Allah, who knows their inner states, who takes the judgment upon them to the exclusion of His prophets and the rulers of His creation.

By this the rulings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded among the servants regarding the hudud and all rights. He informed them that all his judgments are based on what they manifest, while Allah requites according to inner states.

[Section: Words were established to express what is in the soul]

Indeed Allah the Exalted established words among His servants as a means of expressing and indicating what is in their souls. When one of them desires something from another, he makes known his purpose and what is in his soul by his words, and He attached to those intentions and purposes their rulings through the medium of words. He did not attach those rulings to mere inner states without any indication by act or speech, nor to mere words while knowing that the speaker did not intend their meanings and did not comprehend them. Rather He overlooked for the community what its souls whisper, as long as they do not act on it or speak it, and He overlooked for it what it utters in error, forgetfulness, under compulsion, or without knowledge, when it does not intend the meaning of what it said or aim at it. So when intention and verbal or practical indication coincide, the ruling is attached.

This is the principle of the Sharia, and it is among the requirements of Allah's justice, wisdom and mercy. For the thoughts of hearts and the willing of souls do not fall under choice; if rulings were attached to them, there would be the greatest hardship and difficulty upon the community. The mercy and wisdom of Allah the Exalted reject that. Error, forgetfulness, inadvertence, and slips of the tongue saying what the servant does not intend, but intends the opposite, and speaking under compulsion without knowing its implications, are among the necessary features of humanness; a person hardly ever is free of some of it. If a ruling were attached to them, the community would be ruined and would suffer utmost weariness and hardship. So He lifted the accountability for all of that, even the slip of the tongue in utterance due to intense joy, anger or intoxication, as its evidences have passed.

(Section: Attaching the feminine marker to the verb)

Similarly: error, forgetfulness, compulsion, ignorance of the meaning, slips of the tongue, speaking in what is closed (al-ighlaq), and idle oaths. These are ten things for which Allah does not hold His servant accountable when he speaks in a state of any of them, because there was no intention on his part and no resolve of the heart, which is what He holds him accountable for.

(Section: Attaching the feminine marker to the verb)

They say: if the feminine noun's femininity is real, then the feminine marker (ta' al-ta'nith) must attach to the verb; and if it is metaphorical, you have a choice. They claim that the ta' in ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ﴾ ("The Bedouins said") and similar cases marks the feminine plural, which is not real femininity. Yet attaching the ta' in ﴿وَقالَ نِسْوَةٌ﴾ ("And women said") would have been more appropriate, since their femininity is real. They agree that when the verb comes after its feminine subject, the ta' must be present even if the femininity is not real, and they mention no distinction between the verb preceding and following its subject.

Among what may be said to them: if the ta' attaches for the feminine plural, why is it not permitted with the sound masculine plural, as it is permitted with the broken plural? Also, among what may be said to them: if the word for the group is feminine, the word for the plural is masculine, so why is the feminine form observed rather than the masculine?

If you say, "You have a choice: if you observe the feminine form, you make it feminine, and if you observe the masculine form, you make it masculine," it is said to them: this is false, for none of the Arabs said "al-Hindan dhahaba" or "al-A'rab infalaqa" (observing the form of the plural). Thus their reason is invalid. As you see, their reasons have been refuted. Now listen to the secret of the matter and the unveiling of its veil.

The principle in this chapter is that whenever the verb is joined to its subject and no barrier stands between them, the marker is attached, and we do not care whether the femininity is real or metaphorical. So you say: "ṭābat al-thamarah" (the fruit became good) and "jā'at Hind" (Hind came). The exception is when the feminine noun has the sense of another masculine noun, such as al-ḥawādith (the events) and al-ḥadthān (the calamity), and al-arḍ (the earth). Hence the verb came as: "fa-inna al-ḥawādith awdā bihā" (the events have destroyed them). For al-ḥawādith has the sense of al-ḥadthān, and the verb came in "wa-lā arḍ abqala ibqāluhā" (no land has produced its vegetation), since it has the sense of "wa-lā makān abqala ibqāluhā" (no place has produced its vegetation).

When you separate the verb from its subject, the further it is from the subject, the stronger the case for dropping the marker, and the closer it is, the stronger the case for keeping it. If it is placed in the middle, it is intermediate. You say: "ḥaḍara al-qāḍī al-yawma imra'ah" (the judge attended today, a woman), which is better than "ḥaḍarat". In the Qur'an: ﴿وَأخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ ("And the Sound seized those who did wrong").

From here it follows that when the verb comes after its subject, the ta' must be present, whether the sentence is long or short, because when the verb comes after, its subject is a pronoun attached to it, connected as a part to a whole, so the ta' must be present due to the intensity of the connection. When the verb precedes its apparent subject and is joined to it, a verb joined to a pronoun is not like one joined to an apparent noun, because the apparent subject is one word and the verb is another word. So dropping the ta' in "Hind" and "ṭābat al-thamarah" is closer to permissible than in your saying "al-thamarah ṭābat".

If a barrier intervenes between the verb and its subject, dropping the ta' is good, and the more barriers there are, the better dropping it becomes. If the subject is a broken plural, the ta' is used for femininity and dropped for the masculine sense of the word, because it has the status of the singular in that its inflection is like its inflection, and in much speech it functions like a collective noun. If the plural is sound, the masculine must be used, because the singular form of the word is preserved; so you do not say "qālat al-kāfirūn," just as you do not say "qālat al-kāfir," because the word remains as it is and is not altered by the addition of the plural to it.

If it is said: why do you not say "al-A'rab qāla" as you say it when the verb comes first?
It is said: the presence of the ta' was only to observe the sense of plurality. So when you intend that sense, you keep the ta'. If the verb comes after, its deletion is not permitted, because of the attached pronoun. If you do not intend the sense of plurality, you drop the ta' when the verb precedes, and it is not needed when the verb follows, because the pronoun of the male plural subjects refers to a group in meaning, though they are not a plural, since the plural (jam') is a verbal noun of "jama'tu" (I gathered). Whoever says that the masculine form in "dhahaba al-rijāl" and "qāma al-Hindāt" is for the sake of the sense of plurality has erred. As for dropping the ta' in "qāla niswah," it is because it is a collective noun (ism jam'), like ratḥ (a group) and qawm (a people). Were it not that it contains the feminine ta', its verb would have taken the ta' with fatḥah; but you may say "qālat niswah," just as you say "sa'alat qabīlah" and "niswah".

If you say: when the word is preceded by the article al-, namely "al-niswah," the ta' in the verb is better, just as it is in "qālat al-A'rab," because the article al- indicates a known referent, and the noun has already been mentioned, so the verb's state resembles its state when a pronoun in it refers back to a previously mentioned noun because of the al-. In the Noble Qur'an, al-ṣayḥah is understood as referring to the known cry.

If you then ask: if the ta' and its absence are equal in the preceding verb with a feminine subject that is not real, what is the wisdom in its specification with the verb in the story of Shu'ayb, and its omission in the story of Ṣāliḥ: "wa-akhadha alladhīna ẓalamū al-ṣayḥah"?

I say: the Sound (al-ṣayḥah) in the story of Ṣāliḥ has the sense of the punishment and disgrace, since it is linked with His words: ﴿وَمِن خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ إنَّ رَبَّكَ هو القَوِيُّ العَزِيزُ﴾ ("And from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty"). So the Sound becomes an expression for that disgrace and for the punishment mentioned in the verse, and the masculine form is strengthened. This differs from the story of Shu'ayb, where that is not mentioned.

This is the answer of al-Suhayli.

But I have a better answer than this, God willing, which is this: the Sound may be meant as a verbal noun in the sense of shouting, in which case the masculine is good; and it may be meant as the single instance of the verbal noun, in which case the feminine is better. Allah, the Exalted, has informed us of the punishment that struck the people of Shu'ayb with three things, all feminine in form:

First: the quake (al-rajfah), in His words in al-A'rāf: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأصْبَحُوا في دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ﴾ ("So the quake seized them, and they became prostrate in their dwellings").

Second: the cloud (al-ẓullah), in His words: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأخَذَهم عَذابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ﴾ ("So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Cloud seized them").

Third: the Sound (al-ṣayḥah): ﴿وَأخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾.

He combined all three for them: the quake first came upon them, so they went out into the open field fearing the collapse of the buildings upon them; the sun scorched them with its heat; and the cloud was raised for them, so they hastened toward it seeking shade from the sun. Then the punishment descended upon them from it, and in it was the Sound. So mentioning the Sound together with the quake and the cloud is better than mentioning mere shouting, and mentioning the feminine ta' is (what is correct), and Allah knows best.

[Section: On the arrival of the delegation of Banu Asad]

The delegation of Banu Asad, ten men, came to him (ﷺ). Among them were Waabisa ibn Ma'bad and Talha ibn Khuwaylid, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his Companions in the mosque. They spoke, and their spokesman said: "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that Allah alone has no partner, and that you are His servant and His Messenger. We have come to you, O Messenger of Allah, and you did not send any expedition to us, and we are (speaking) for those behind us." Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Then Allah revealed to His Messenger: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, Allah bestows a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17].

Among the things they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about on that day were: augury (al-'iyafa), soothsaying (al-kahana), and striking pebbles (darb al-hasa). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them from all of that. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are matters we used to practise in the Jahiliyyah. Tell us, is there a trait that remains?" He said: "And what is it?" They said: "The line (al-khatt)." He said: "A prophet from among the prophets taught it, so whoever happens upon knowledge like his, will know (it)."

(Section)

The servant stands between a favour from Allah upon him and a proof from Him against him, and he is never free of either. Thus the religious ruling includes both His favour and His proof. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah certainly conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 164].

And He said: ﴿Rather, Allah confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17].

And He said: ﴿Then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

The created (kawni) ruling also includes His favour and His proof. So when He decrees for him a created ruling accompanied by the connection of the religious ruling to it, it is a favour upon him; and if the religious does not accompany it, it is a proof from Him against him.

Likewise, His religious ruling, when His created ruling is connected to it, His enabling him to carry it out is a favour from Him upon him; and if it is stripped of His created ruling, it becomes a proof from Him against him. Thus favour lies in the conjunction of one of the two rulings with its counterpart, and proof lies in the separation of one of them from the other. So every knowledge accompanied by action that pleases Allah, glorified is He, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every apparent and hidden power accompanied by carrying out His pleasure and His commands is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every state accompanied by an effect in supporting His religion and calling to it is a favour from Him; otherwise it is a proof.

Every wealth joined with spending in the way of Allah and in obedience to Him, not seeking reward or thanks, is a favour from Allah upon him; otherwise it is a proof.

Every leisure joined with occupation with what the Lord wants from His servant is a favour upon him; otherwise it is a proof.

Every acceptance among people, and esteem and love for him, that is connected with humility before the Lord, lowliness and brokenness, awareness of the fault of the self and of deeds, and offering sincere advice to creation, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every insight and admonition, reminder and instruction from the instructions of the Truth, glorified is He, addressed to the servant, that is connected with lesson, increase in intellect, and knowledge in faith, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every state with Allah, the Exalted, or station connected with traveling to Allah and preferring His desire over the servant's desire, is a favour from Allah. But if it is accompanied by stopping at it, contentment with it, and preferring its requirement out of the pleasure of the self in it, its tranquillity in it, and its inclination toward it, then it is a proof from Allah against him.

So let the servant reflect on this most momentous point, and distinguish between the places of favours and trials, and proofs and blessings, for how often this becomes confused for the elite among people and the adherents of the spiritual path. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
